title: plain language
name: Plain language
rule: Write labels and instructions in plain language that mirrors how users talk about the information.

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Labels/instructions use ordinary words for the asked data.
fail_when: Copy requires unexplained jargon to know what to enter.
overview: Labels and instructions use ordinary words that match how users talk.
apply_when: Naming fields and writing instructions for data people must enter.
not_when: Domain terms users already use daily in that specialist product.
agent_hint: Mirror user language in labels; avoid unexplained jargon for the asked data.
description: Write labels and instructions in plain language that mirrors how users talk about the information they must provide. Ordinary words should be enough to know what belongs in the field without a glossary. Apply when naming fields and writing entry instructions for everyday data. Fail copy that requires unexplained jargon before someone can tell what to enter.
